no-var  This is a `var` declaration, which is function-scoped and hoisted rather than block-scoped. The binding exists from the top of the enclosing function, so it is readable above the line that declares it and it leaks out of the block it looks like it belongs to: a `var` inside an `if` is still in scope after the `if` ends. A reader tracing what happens on one pass has to hold every `continue` above their position in mind, because any of them may have skipped the code they are looking at, and in a `for` loop the update expression still runs while the rest of the body does not.
